question: Pulseless Electrical Activity (PEA) and Asystole are shockable rhythms that should be treated with immediate defibrillation during Advanced Life Support.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is FALSE. PEA and Asystole are non-shockable rhythms. Defibrillation is indicated only for VF and pVT. For PEA/Asystole, continue high-quality CPR and address reversible causes (the 4Hs and 4Ts).
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. PEA and Asystole are NON-shockable rhythms. Only Ventricular Fibrillation (VF) and pulseless Ventricular Tachycardia (pVT) are shockable. Defibrillating a non-shockable rhythm wastes time and harms the patient.
